chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Had kindness (rifq) been a visible creature, there would not have been, among what Allah created, anything more beautiful than it.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the beauty of kindness?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni transmits this narration through the chain of Jabir al-Ju'fi to Imam al-Baqir, highlighting the ontological beauty of *rifq* (gentleness) as a divine attribute. This hadith elevates kindness from mere social etiquette to a cosmic aesthetic ideal, suggesting that its essence surpasses all physical creations in visual and spiritual splendor. It serves as a foundational text in Shia ethics for understanding how prophetic character reflects the divine nature.
